transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

I guess... I got written up at work last week. I'm a cashier, and... I don't know, I just keep getting stuck doing things at the register. Things that don't really fit what's happening. 

Like... I'll start tapping the scanner in a pattern. Or I'll just freeze. My hand will just hover over the cash drawer and I just stop, while the customer is standing right there waiting. So... that's why I'm here.
When you start tapping the scanner like that, do you feel a sudden urge or buildup right before it happens?
No... I don't really notice anything like that. It's not like an urge. I just... I'm just doing it. There isn't really a warning.
When you freeze at the register, are you aware of what is happening around you and able to hear people talking to you?
I... I don't know. I guess I hear them, but... it's just noise. I'm not really paying attention. I'm just... stuck.
Do you ever feel able to hold back or stop the tapping or freezing for a short time if you try?

I... no. If I could hold it back, I probably wouldn't have gotten written up last week. 

Like I said, I just... I get stuck doing those things at the register. The tapping, or... just freezing there with my hand out while they wait. I don't really know how to stop it. It just happens.
Do these episodes tend to happen when you're under stress or after something upsetting happens?
I'm not sure. I haven't really noticed a connection like that. Work is... just work. I don't think it has anything to do with being upset. It just happens when it happens.
Before the tapping or freezing happens, do you ever get a sudden uncomfortable feeling or urge that builds up until you do it?
No, I don't think so. I don't feel anything building up. I just... do it.
Right before the tapping or freezing starts, do you feel an inner tension or sense that you have to do it to relieve discomfort?
No. I don't feel any tension. I already said, I don't feel anything before it happens. It just... starts.
When these episodes start, can you stop yourself from doing them if you try?
I don't know. I haven't really... tried to stop it. It just happens.
Do the tapping or freezing episodes come on suddenly and last only a few seconds each time?
I'm not really sure... I haven't timed it or anything. I don't pay that much attention to it.
Do you ever get unwanted, repetitive thoughts or images that make you feel you have to do the tapping or freezing?
No. I don't get thoughts like that. It's just... I just do it. There's no reason for it.
During these episodes, do you ever feel like you are not yourself or like you are watching yourself from outside?
No... I don't think so. I'm just... right there. It's just me.
Do these episodes ever happen when you’re not at work or not at the register?

Not really. It's... mostly at the register. That's why I had to come in, actually. I just keep getting stuck doing things that... don't fit the moment. Like tapping the scanner in a pattern, or... just freezing with my hand over the cash drawer while the customer is waiting. I... well, I got written up for it last week. So... yeah, mostly at work.
During these episodes, do you ever lose awareness of what is happening around you or seem unresponsive to other people?
No... I hear what's going on. I know they're there. I just... I guess I just don't answer them right away.
Have you ever had any spells where you black out or lose time?
No... I don't think so. I remember what happens.
During these episodes, do you ever feel like you’re in a trance or not fully in control of yourself?
I don't think so. It's not... I wouldn't call it a trance. I'm still there. I just... get stuck, like I said.
During these episodes, do you ever feel like something else has taken over you or is controlling your actions?
No... nothing like that. It's just me. I'm still in control... I just can't always get moving.
During these episodes, do you ever have trouble moving part of your body, like your arm or hand, even though you want to?
No. My arms and hands work fine. I just... I don't have trouble moving them.
During these episodes, do you ever feel unable to move your body even though you want to?
No... if I want to move, I can move. It's not like I'm paralyzed. I just... sometimes I just don't.
Are you aware of doing the tapping or freezing when it happens?

Yeah... I'm aware. I just get stuck. Like at the register... I'll be tapping the scanner in this pattern, or... I'll just freeze with my hand over the open cash drawer. I know the customer is standing right there waiting. It just doesn't fit the moment, but... I do it anyway. I actually got written up for it last week. That's... that's why I came in.
Do the tapping or freezing episodes start and stop very suddenly, like an on-off switch?
I don't really know. I haven't... I haven't noticed if it's exactly like that. It just happens.

final_diagnosis.reason: The presentation is most consistent with dissociative motor disorder (F44.4): the patient has recurrent episodes of apparent motor inhibition/freezing and patterned tapping that occur in a work setting, are experienced as involuntary, and lead to occupational impairment. However, the interview did not confirm classic tic features (premonitory urge, suppressibility, brief stereotyped spells) or a clear dissociative trance/possession state. F44.7 was considered because of the freezing-like episodes, but there is no evidence of multiple dissociative symptom types or broader mixed dissociative presentation.
